physical.title: figure
physical.summary: Painted wooden figure representing a Chin man. Such painted wooden figures (with some metal parts) depicted 'types' of Burmese people. They were popularly made for the European market in Burma. The figure is dressed in a long mauve longyi, exposing one leg which has been elaborately tattooed from the shin up to the hip, as well as across the lower abdomen. Carrying such decoration was a mark of honour and, indeed, a rite of passage, for young Burmese men up until the last century. The figure carries a hat (which is made of metal) and is slung over his right shoulder. He wears a turbanned headdress which is tied up the side.

physical.title: puppet
physical.summary: Painted wooden marionette of a Burmese princess, or 'minthamee'. The figure is dressed in court attire and wears a textile in the 'acheik' (wave) design distinctive of the Mandalay court. However, these figures post-date that period by a short time. The court attire is inter-woven with metal thread and embellished with steams of sequins. The lower garment is claret coloured. The upper is green and white. The facial features are carefully painted, including the folds of skin on the neck. The puppet's hair is probably horse hair. As is typical of the dress for an aristocratic woman, there is a long train. The puppet's ankles are attached to it at the back. The train severely restricted the movement of the individual. The figure is attached to a wooden handling frame by cotton threads, with which it would have been manipulated. The figure is one of a pair: 2005.0618.1 & 2.
